lesson.name: Learn the Queen's Gambit Cambridge Springs and Orthodox Defense
lesson.description: Learn the key ideas for both sides in the tactical Cambridge Springs Defense and the solid Orthodox Defense. These openings have been played by World Champions for more than a century!

a good capture.}) 7. Bxd8 {Great move! How can you win back the queen?} Bb4+ {
[%wrong White is winning. Try to find a strong check to turn things around.]

{When White plays an early Bd3, Black can win a tempo for the famous
"Capablanca's Freeing Manuever." What should Black play to trade pieces and
reach a safe position?} 8... dxc4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find
it.] [%hint Trade and attack the d3 bishop.]} (8... h6 $5 {This is a fine move,
but not the traditional weapon preferred by World Champion Capablanca. What
was his favorite move here?}) (8... b6 $5 {This is a fine move, but not the
traditional weapon preferred by World Champion Capablanca. What was his
favorite move here?}) (8... a6 $5 {This is a fine move, but not the
traditional weapon preferred by World Champion Capablanca. What was his
favorite move here?}) 9. Bxc4 {Good start! Black's only serious problem is the
cramped position. How can you force at least one trade to ease the cramping?}
Nd5 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find it.] [%hint Force White to
trade the dark-squared bishop.]} (9... h6 $5 {This is a fine move, but not the
traditional weapon preferred by World Champion Capablanca. What was his
favorite move here to force trades?}) (9... b5 $5 {This is a fine move, but
not the traditional weapon preferred by World Champion Capablanca. What was
his favorite move here to force trades?}) (9... b6 $5 {This is a fine move,
but not the traditional weapon preferred by World Champion Capablanca. What
was his favorite move here to force trades?}) (9... a6 $5 {This is a fine move,
but not the traditional weapon preferred by World Champion Capablanca. What
was his favorite move here to force trades?}) (9... Nh5 $2 10. Bxe7 {This
forces a trade, but the knight on h5 is poorly placed. Find another way to
execute the same idea.}) (9... Ng4 $2 10. Bf4 {White is better. Try again.})
10. Bxe7 {Great job! What capture should you play next?} Qxe7 {[%wrong White
wins material. Try again.] [%hint Recapture and develop a piece] Well played!
Black has a solid position.} (10... Nxe7 $2 11. O-O {Black will have a
difficult time in this cramped position. Try to find a better move.}) (10...
Nxc3 $2 11. Bxd8 {White meets Nxd1 with Be7 and an advantage. Try again.}) *

{How did World Champion Kramnik break the pin on c3?} 11. a3 {[%wrong There's
a stronger move. Try to attack the b4-bishop.] [%hint Attack the b4-bishop.]} (
11. e4 $5 {This is a good move, but Kramnik preferred to attack the b4-bishop.
How did he do it?}) (11. Bd3 $5 {This is a good move, but Kramnik preferred to
break the pin on his knight. What did he play to attack Black's bishop?}) 11...
Bxc3 {Great move! How should you recapture?} 12. bxc3 {[%wrong There's a
better option. Try to find a good capture.] [%hint Recapture and don't lose
more than a pawn.]} (12. Rxc3 $2 Nxc3 {Black wins material. Try to find a
better capture.}) (12. Qxc3 $2 Nxc3 {Black wins the queen. Try to find a
better capture.}) 12... Qxa3 {Good choice! White has sacrificed a pawn for
good central control and a lead in development. How should you start an attack?
} 13. e4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find a way to attack the
d5-knight.] [%hint Force Black's knight from the center.] Well played! White
has a strong attack. We will revisit Kramnik-Bruzon 2006 in the next challenge.
} (13. Bd3 $5 {This is a good developing move, but Kramnik preferred to force
away the d5-knight. How did he do it?}) (13. c4 $2 Ne7 {Black is OK. Try to
find a better way to attack the d5-knight.}) (13. Bc4 $2 b5 {Black is OK. Try
to find a stronger way to attack d5.}) *

{What strong sacrifice did Kramnik play to start a winning attack?} 26. Bxf7+ {
[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find a winning sacrifice to expose the
black king.] [%hint Sacrifice to draw out the black king.]} (26. Nf5 $2 Nde5 {
White is only slightly better. Try to find a strong sacrifice instead.}) (26.
e5 $2 Ndf8 {White is only slightly better. Try to find a strong sacrifice
instead.}) 26... Kxf7 {Great move! How can you keep checking the black king?} 27.
Qa2+ {[%wrong There's a better option. Look for a good check and try again.] 
[%hint Check on the a2-g8 diagonal.]} Kf8 {Well played! How should you keep
attacking the black king?} 28. Ne6+ {[%wrong Black is doing well. Try to find
a good check.] [%hint Fork Black's king and queen.]} (28. Nf5 $5 {This is a
strong move, but Kramnik preferred to check with the knight. How did he do it?}
) 28... Rxe6 {Good move! What's next?} 29. Qxe6 {[%wrong Black is winning. Try
to find a good capture.] [%hint Capture an undefended piece.]} Ne7 {Well
played! How did Kramnik lift a rook into the attack?} 30. Re3 {[%wrong There's
a better move. Try to find the best way to bring a rook into the attack.] 
[%hint Lift your e1-rook so it can soon reach f3.]} (30. Bd6 $5 Qg5 {White is
doing well, but Kramnik preferred to bring his e1-rook into the attack. How
did he do it?}) (30. e5 $5 {White is doing well, but Kramnik preferred to
bring his e1-rook into the attack. How did he do it?}) (30. Rd3 $2 Nf6 {
White is only slightly better. Try to lift the other rook into your attack.})
30... Ke8 {Great move! Where should the rook head next?} 31. Rf3 {[%wrong
There's a better move. Try to find the best square for your e3-rook.] [%hint
Threaten mate on f7.]} (31. e5 $5 {This is a good move, but Kramnik preferred
to control f7 with a rook. How should you do that?}) (31. h3 $5 {This is a
good move, but Kramnik preferred to control f7 with a rook. How should you do
that?}) (31. Rg3 $5 {This is a good move, but Kramnik preferred to control f7
with the rook. How should you do that?}) 31... Qh5 {Well played! What did
Kamnik play to threaten mate and convince his opponent to resign?} 32. Bd6 {
[%wrong There's a better move to force mate. Try to find a way to attack the
pinned knight on e7.] [%hint Attack Black's pinned knight on e7 and threaten
mate.] Well done! Black has no good defense against mate and resigned in
Kramnik-Bruzon 2006.} (32. h3 $5 {White is winning, but there's a stronger
move to threaten an immediate mate. Try to find Kramnik's choice.}) (32. Rf5 $2
Qxd1# {That's mate. Try again.}) (32. Rd2 $5 {White is winning, but there's a
stronger move to threaten an immediate mate. Try to find Kramnik's choice.}) *
